# 高上玉皇本行集經(一)

**ID:** KR5a0010
**Custom ID:** ZB5a0010

**Editions:** SJB, ZHDZ

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A three-juan five-section scripture on the origin and transformative activity of Yùhuáng 玉皇 ("The Jade Emperor"), the supreme deity of popular and late-imperial Daoism. The scripture is set in the Qīngwēi 清微 heaven — the highest of the Three Pure Realms and the seat of the Qīngwēi-school pantheon — where Yuánshǐ tiānzūn 元始天尊 preaches the "pure, untainted, non-dual doctrine" (清淨真一不二法門) to an assembly including Yùhuáng himself. Yùhuáng then multiplies his body to address all regions of the cosmos, recombines, and narrates his own cosmic biography: his origin as an avatar of the Most High Dàojūn 道君, his 3,200 *kalpa* cultivation, his ascent to the rank of Golden Immortal (金仙) under the Mahāyāna title Rúlái 如來 ("King of Pure and Spontaneous Awakening," 淨覺自然王如來), and his consequent teaching of the true *dàshèng* 大乘 doctrine to the host of bodhisattvas. The text concludes with an enumeration of the thirty wondrous merits attendant upon reverent recitation — including the destruction of the *Tiěwéi* 鐵圍 iron-ringed hells, the abolition of the sea of suffering, the breaking of the great prisons, the subjugation of evil *mó* 魔 demons, and thirty blessings ranging from "praise by the host of immortals" to "ascent in broad daylight."

Structurally the three juan are divided into five *pǐn*: 清微天宮神通品 ("The Miracles of the Qīngwēi Heavenly Palace"), the scripture's opening and revelation-scene, and four further sections treating the Jade Emperor's past lives, cosmic preaching, salvational power, and the merits of recitation. Juan 2 contains an embedded revelation of the *Língbǎo chìshū yùpiān zhēnwén* 靈寶赤書玉篇真文 ("True Writs in Vermilion Writing on Jade Tablets") drawn directly from *[DZ 22 Yuánshǐ wǔlǎo chìshū yùpiān zhēnwén tiānshū jīng 元始五老赤書玉篇真文天書經](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0022)*, integrating the Jade Emperor cult textually with the early Língbǎo corpus.

**Abstract**

The *Yùhuáng běnxíng jíjīng* was not in circulation before the thirteenth century. The earliest documentary anchor is the bibliographical entry in the Fùzhì 附志 (1249) supplement to Cháo Gōngwǔ's 晁公武 *Jùnzhāi dúshū zhì* 郡齋讀書志 (item 1161), which records an edition printed in 1240 by the Chéngtiān língyìng guàn 承天靈應觀 in Hángzhōu, itself based on a Sichuan recension (蜀本), with a preface by Chéng Gōngxǔ 程公許 (*jìnshì* 1211). The Chéngtiān língyìng guàn is recorded in *Xiánchún Lín'ān zhì* 咸淳臨安志 75.8a; it was a cult-centre dedicated to Zǐtóng dìjūn 梓潼帝君 (i.e. Wénchāng 文昌) and received its name in 1236. Quotations of the scripture appear in a number of Yuán-era Daoist works, notably DZ 103 *Yùqīng wújí zǒngzhēn Wénchāng dàdòng xiānjīng zhù* 5.17a, 25b (Wèi Qí, 1310 — the commentary on [DZ 5](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0005)).

Kristofer Schipper's entry in *The Taoist Canon* (2004) 2:1097, §3.B.7 ("The Qingwei School"), identifies the *Yùhuáng jīng* as a scripture of the Qīngwēi 清微 school — the late-Sòng / Yuán Daoist movement that treated itself as successor to the Shénxiāo 神霄 and developed Thunder-rite (*léifǎ* 雷法) liturgies. Although the *Yùhuáng jīng* itself does not mention the Qīngwēi school by name, the related *Gāoshàng Yùhuáng mǎnyuàn bǎozhàn* 高上玉皇滿願寳懺 (DZ 194) explicitly invokes the Qīngwēi patriarchs, securing the affiliation. The extent to which the *Yùhuáng jīng* may be a reconstitution of the lost early-Língbǎo *Língbǎo zhēnwén dùrén běnxíng miàojīng* 靈寳真文度人本行妙經 (Lagerwey, *Wu-shang pi-yao*, p. 265) is difficult to determine.

The frontmatter brackets the composition notBefore 1180 (latest plausible late-Southern-Sòng window, consistent with both the undated textual anchor and the Qīngwēi-school chronology) / notAfter 1240 (the Hangzhou printing), with dynasty 南宋. The catalog meta lists no attributed author for DZ 10; *persons* is accordingly empty. (The DZ 11 commentary is spuriously attributed to Zhāng Liáng 張良, d. 187 BCE — see [KR5a0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0011).)
